Could you add some output of what the associations made are?  For some reason I was under the impression that the fansensor app held the inventory interfaces for fans and not EM.

You are correct -- this change goes with some tweaks to how FanSensor handles inventory item associations. That PR has not been pushed yet, but will soon -- likely tomorrow.

I still have more cleanup to do across a few PRs I got started on gerrit today, but I'll aim to update the commit message with a "TESTED' section showing how things look in object mapper with a set of these associations in play.
What is your timeline to fill the TESTED section?

Ah, I totally forgot about that bit in the commit message.

I ran into some local build machine issues Friday, but I'll give it another go this next week and update with a copy/pate of some dbus tree data showing the cooling/cooled_by associations in action.

Got things working again, TESTED section added. I'll give this another look tomorrow to fix the merge conflict.

Do folks want to see more specific details than what I added already?

> Do folks want to see more specific details than what I added already?

Commit message could be expanded to go into more detail as to the fan inventory.

I could be wrong here but i feel like that's one of the remaining points to be resolved.

If EM can have a fan inventory with `cooling` / `cooled_by`, where does that leave Fan sensor daemon?

I grepped through dbus-sensors and could not find `cooling` / `cooled_by` in there.

It looks like you have a patch for that
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/82436

so it would be good to have that linked in the commit message.

It would be nice if we do not end up in a situation where the fan inventory is held by EM for some boards and then held by fan sensor on other boards. Maybe it could be done but discussing these tradeoffs can be part of a commit message.

Such an implementation may lead to code drift. If someone needs to add another association to a fan inventory item or another property to it's interface then that would need to be done in 2 repositories.

meta uses `Type: Board` for a fanboard 
https://github.com/openbmc/entity-manager/blob/master/configurations/meta/yv4/fanboard/yosemite4_fanboard_fsc_max_adc_ti_led_nxp_ons_efuse_max.json

so having a `Type: Board` config with the `cooling` port/association record and having the fans simply copy that would be a way to avoid these issues.

So conceptually the `Board` is `cooling` some other item (e.g. chassis) and there are fan(s) on that board. fan sensor can then go and look at the association defined for the board and copy that to create the same association on the fan inventory item.

Now if the `Board` in question actually exists or if it's just the fan is more of a conceptual question to me and should not make a difference to the implementation.

The issue with that idea is that we would be creating a `cooling` association on a `Board` inventory item.

However i feel like creating such an association is less of a problem than distributing a specific inventory across multiple services.

I assume there is some reason for fan sensor to hold the fan inventory. It can go via hwmon to figure out if the fan in question is actually there (tach input / pwm output), so it has some role in device detection / initialization.

Let me know what you think of these ideas, i may be wrong since i don't know much about the design intent behind who's holding which inventory.

>I could be wrong here but i feel like that's one of the remaining points to be resolved.

I agree. 

So far, the current method has been the only way I've managed to get any fan items to show up in redfish/bmcweb's Fan Inventory, but we're not tied to that solution.

I still have more experimenting and digging around to do to figure out why adding an Inventory.Item.Fan interface to fan paths on the xyz.openbmc_project.FanSensors dbus wasn't enough to get them picked up like I initially thought it would. 

I figured if we accepted this code as it is today, we'd end up doing a later pass later to reconcile and 'nice up' how Fan Inventory is handled.

With a bit of guidance, I'm happy to get it figured out now. 

I hadn't seen that fan 'board' example -- that's useful for my understanding. 

I'm not fundamentally against having a "fan board" and keeping the fan Inventory.Item stuff under xyz.openbmc_project.FanSensors. I'll do some thinking and experimenting and come back to this.

Thanks a ton for the in-depth writeup!
Could you also update https://github.com/openbmc/entity-manager/blob/master/docs/associations.md that documents which associations EM can create itself?

This update goes with an update to the dbus-sensors/FanSensor daemon to add the appropriate associations for each fan discovered.

The FanSensor change is needed for redfish-core to pickup fans exposed this way.

There will also be some example Entity-Manager code uploaded for discussion (those PRs pending)
*a working entity-manager config example
Definitely.
Solid suggestion. Accepted.

Here's the FanSensor modifications to get this working: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/82436

by 'working' I mean to get PWM and FanTach sensors (separately exposed, and linked to chassis through downstream port(s) in EMConfig) reporting in the webUI sensors page, and showing fan inventory items on the inventory page.

I think I'm about 95% of the way there, but will want some community input to help make sure I've got the structures organized in a way that makes sense.

I'll be back on this tomorrow to update entity-manger documentation for cooling/cooled_by and to see about adding some example entity-manager code for further discussion.

Then I plan to ask around for folks' thoughts on Discord.
If fansensor is already creating the cooling/cooled_by associations, what are the EM associations for?  Are they multiple hop associations? Can bmcweb handle that?

As I understand it, this is the bit that associates a chassis with a 'type:fan' entity (probe + exposes) called out in an EM json. 

The FanSensor parts association records (after the dbus-sensors PR is accepted) uses the associations called out here to link sensors to the chasis so they'll show up in redfish/bmcweb on the sensors page.

The 'type:fan' entity seems to be needed to get a 'fan' item to show up in the webui inventory page, but I'm still experimenting around there to get a handle on the finer details on the display there.

The EM config change in question already has a +2, but I'm waiting for this dbus-sensors PR it depends on to get turned into a +2 so they can merge together, since there's technically a dependency (even if it's not enforced by anything). 

78023: hwmontempsensor: add support for tmp1075 temp sensors | https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/78023

It went went a sibling PR that was already merged, but this one hit a merge conflict that didn't get noticed for awhile. Brought it up in discord, so should get noticed sooner than later.

Associations.md has now been updated with info about cooled_by/cooling associations  for further discussion.

Schema has also been updated to recognize the 'FanPort' boolean. I noticed some unit test stuff surrounding PowerPort, so I'll probably look into setting up something similar for FanPort next week.
Setting type: fan for an entity seems to be a requirement for getting 'fan' items to show up in fan inventory presented through redfish/bmcweb's inventory page.
Your assumption is correct. Also setting this allows the EM Config validation to succeed.

I do not like `Type` field to be templated or otherwise variable.
`Type` field is what is used by people to find the schema and create the dbus interfaces name.

So for both purposes `Type` should be fixed. Maybe topology schema needs to be reworked. Not sure how to go about this but could we extend `DownstreamPort` with an optional `ConnectsToName` property.

From my understanding the ports are only consumed by EM to create the associations, so we should be free to make changes there?

I would wholeheartedly agree if we were starting from scratch -- but a complicating factor is that current association handling for the powering/powered_by example in association.md explicitly says

>the Type fields for those ports match up with the ConnectsToType field from the PSUs.

https://github.com/openbmc/entity-manager/blob/master/docs/associations.md


and there's a small handful of EMConfigs using it in templated form as described today:

https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Aopenbmc%2Fentity-manager%20path%3A%2F%5Econfigurations%5C%2F%2F%20downstream&type=code

I think if we changed how that works for cooling/cooled_by, we'd probably want to change it for powering/powered_by too -- but I'm not sure what the appetite for backtesting changes there would be.
